Project type and purpose: Real-time chat application enabling one-on-one communication between users via a vibrant and engaging web interface.
Programming language(s) and primary fram: Frontend: React with Material-UI for a vibrant design. Backend: Node.js with Express and WebSocket library (e.g., Socket.IO or ws).
Project scope and complexity: The project involves building a real-time, two-user chat application with a focus on delivering a visually appealing and intuitive user experience. It includes handling WebSocket connections, message persistence, and basic user interface components.
Core functionality requirements: User Authentication: Simple username/password or social login.
Real-time Chat: Sending and receiving text messages via WebSocket.
Vibrant UI: Attractive and modern design using React and Material-UI.
Message History: Displaying a history of messages between users.
Online Status: Indicating when a user is online or offline.
Typing Indicator: Showing when the other user is typing a message.
Notifications: Sound or visual notifications for new messages.
Data storage needs: Local JSON file storage for user accounts and chat history to keep it simple.
External integrations: No external API integrations are included.
Security considerations: Basic input sanitization to prevent script injection. Password hashing for user authentication.
Story: User A logs into the chat application with a username and password. Upon successful login, they are presented with a list of available users to chat with. User A selects User B from the list. A chat window opens, displaying any previous conversation history between the two users. User A types a message and presses Enter. The message is immediately sent to User B via WebSocket, and User B sees the message appear in their chat window in real-time. User B starts typing a response, and User A sees a 'User B is typing...' indicator. User B sends their message, and User A receives it instantly. This back-and-forth continues seamlessly, providing a real-time chat experience. The chat history is stored locally in a JSON file.
